The certificate log verify processor verifies cryptographic integrity attributes
on log records. For each log record it recomputes a canonical JSON payload
(RFC 8785 / JCS) and checks `audit.integrity.value` against a configured HMAC
key and/or certificate public key. Failed records can optionally be marked or
dropped, and verification failures can be written to a dead-letter storage
extension.

The processor is designed for use with the [OpenTelemetry Audit Logging
signal](https://github.com/apeirora/opentelemetry-specification/tree/auditing/specification/audit)
and is the verification counterpart to
[`signingprocessor`](../signingprocessor).

> **Note:** This first PR donates the component skeleton only (README, config,
> factory, and passthrough processor). Concrete verification logic lands in a
> follow-up PR per the
> [donation guide](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/docs/new-components.md#donation).

## Configuration

For complete examples of all supported configurations see
[testdata/config.yaml](./testdata/config.yaml).
For invalid configuration examples used in tests see
[testdata/config_invalid.yaml](./testdata/config_invalid.yaml).

```yaml
processors:
  certificatelogverify:
    # Verification mode. Only "sync" is supported. Default: sync.
    mode: sync

    # How to handle verification failures. Default: strict.
    # - strict: drop failed records and fail the batch
    # - mark:   annotate failed records and continue
    failure_mode: strict

    # Label stamped onto each verified record. Default: default.
    verification_profile: default

    # HMAC key file (standard base64-encoded). Required unless cert_file or
    # k8s_secret provides key material.
    hmac_key_file: /etc/otelcol/hmac.key

    # PEM certificate for asymmetric signature verification (RS256, RS512,
    # ES256, EdDSA). Optional when only HMAC is used.
    # cert_file: /etc/otelcol/cert.pem

    # Kubernetes Secret key material (alternative to local files).
    # k8s_secret:
    #   name:      verify-secret
    #   namespace: default
    #   hmac_key_entry: hmac.key
    #   cert_key:       tls.crt

    # Optional hash-chain continuity checks.
    hash_chain:
      enabled: false
      # storage: file_storage

    # Optional dead-letter queue for verification failures.
    dead_letter:
      enabled: false
      # storage: file_storage
      # key_prefix: audit_verify_dlq/
```

## Key material sources

| Source | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hmac_key_file` | Local file containing a standard base64-encoded HMAC secret. |
| `cert_file` | Local PEM certificate used to verify asymmetric signatures. |
| `k8s_secret` | Kubernetes Secret providing `hmac_key_entry` and/or `cert_key`. |

At least one of these sources must be configured.

## Output attributes

The concrete verification implementation (follow-up PR) stamps per-record
outcome attributes such as verification status and machine-readable reason
codes. Integrity attributes consumed for verification are:

| Attribute | Location | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.integrity.value` | log record | Base64-encoded signature or HMAC produced by `signingprocessor`. |
| `audit.integrity.algorithm` | resource | JWA/IANA algorithm identifier (e.g. `RS256`, `HMAC-SHA256`). |
| `audit.integrity.certificate` | resource | Certificate fingerprint or full DER reference (asymmetric only). |

## Example pipeline

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:

processors:
  certificatelogverify:
    mode: sync
    failure_mode: strict
    hmac_key_file: /etc/otelcol/hmac.key
    cert_file: /etc/otelcol/cert.pem

exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: audit-sink:4317

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers:  [otlp]
      processors: [certificatelogverify]
      exporters:  [otlp]
```
